name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
role: President of Syria (2025–); former leader of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (as Abu Mohammad al-Jolani)
summary: Al-Sharaa moved from leading an al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group to governing Syria as a Sunni Islamist-rooted but pragmatic president. His record shows a centralised presidential system with Islamic jurisprudence as the main source of law, a state monopoly on arms, a turn to free markets and foreign investment, and a security-first, non-confrontational line toward Israel.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Al Jazeera reported that he called the Golan Heights occupied and said a deal would not compromise Syria's right to them; the report is a paraphrase, and he did not discuss consent of the population.

ban-cartels.rationale: The declaration he issued says the economy rests on fair competition and bans monopolies.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Article 30 requires assembly approval, but its membership is presidentially controlled.

central-planning.rationale: In the same 2026 speech he described leaving the socialist (state-run) model for a free-market system, which rejects central planning.

consent-of-governed.rationale: In September 2025 he said his government must reflect the voice of the people; he did not otherwise state a theory of legitimacy.

decide-locally.rationale: He has backed a strong centralised state and said the coast cannot be governed separately from other regions.

democracy-best.rationale: He praised popular choice but personally retained a legislature selected through controlled committees and his appointments.

elective-rulers.rationale: He promised elected leadership after transition but continued exercising office through appointment rather than popular election.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: His Constitutional Declaration lists protected rights and requires two-thirds to amend, but amendment starts only on his proposal before an assembly he partly appoints, and it criminalises glorifying the old regime.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The declaration he issued gives citizens equal rights and duties regardless of race, religion, gender or lineage, but it also requires a Muslim president and restricts rights on security and morals grounds.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: His government pressed the Kurdish-led SDF militarily in early 2026 before an integration agreement, and he rejected an isolated coastal authority; he did not frame force as a response to secession specifically.

gradual-change.rationale: At the UN in September 2025 he said Syrians had no choice but to organise militarily to oust the regime and that his government then dissolved all previous civil and military formations; he defends the armed overthrow. He now sets a five-year transition before elections, but that is a timetable for elections, not a stated preference for gradual social change, so low.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Under the declaration he issued, the president is supreme commander of the armed forces and declares mobilization with National Security Council approval.

indirect-election.rationale: He had two-thirds of the transitional assembly chosen by electoral bodies under his control, but called this a stopgap until Syria is ready for elections and called people choosing their leaders a basic principle.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitutional declaration he issued makes Islamic jurisprudence the main source of legislation; asked about applying Islamic law he deferred to experts, and the declaration also keeps rights guarantees, so it falls short of full scriptural law.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: At the 2026 Arab Media Summit he described Syria moving from a socialist economic model to a free-market system with a larger private-sector role.

minority-language-support.rationale: In January 2026 he issued a decree making Kurdish a national language alongside Arabic that schools may teach, and banning ethnic or linguistic discrimination.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He called for a strong centralised state and said the coast cannot be run by an independent authority; the Kurdish autonomy rejection is reported in paraphrase. His January 2026 decree gives cultural, not territorial, rights.

national-resource-control.rationale: His Constitutional Declaration makes all natural wealth public property for the state to exploit; he has not spoken to foreign control as such.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He sought eventual removal of foreign bases through negotiations, while temporarily legalising remaining foreign presences.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: In September 2025 he said he might discuss the Golan if Israel de-escalates, and in July 2026 that a security deal would not give up Syria's right to the Golan; the statements point both ways.

party-commands-army.rationale: Article 9 of the Constitutional Declaration he issued (March 2025) calls the army a professional national institution that only the state may create, and bars any person or group from forming armed units; at the UN in September 2025 he said his government dissolved all previous military formations (his own HTS included) into restructured state institutions, and in August 2026 he insisted on state control of arms. Command by a ruling party contradicts this; no ruling party exists.

party-controls-media.rationale: The declaration he issued guarantees press and information freedom, and he said media should avoid politicization; no ruling party exists to control it.

people-in-arms.rationale: He advocated professional national security forces and disarming factions into one state army.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He explicitly rejected dividing executive authority into religious or ethnic quotas.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He said Syria should rebuild its laws relying on its millennia-old cultural heritage, a leaning rather than a stated priority on preserving traditions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Article 16 protects property, allowing compensated public-interest expropriation.

refugee-return.rationale: In his interview with The New Arab he said refugees have a right to return voluntarily and with dignity and that most Syrians would come back if conditions allowed. He did not mention descendants.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He rejected sacralising human interpretations and urged revising inherited Islamist doctrines for changing conditions.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He has said Syria's claim to the Golan Heights remains, but has not demanded its return and is pursuing a security agreement without confrontation.

right-to-secede.rationale: The declaration he issued calls Syria indivisible and criminalizes calls for secession; in November 2025 he said the coast cannot be run by an independent authority isolated from other regions.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Ordered an inquiry into the 2025 coastal killings of Alawites, but prosecutions of the forces involved remained limited; mixed.

separate-church-state.rationale: The declaration he issued requires the president to be Muslim and sets Islamic jurisprudence as the main source of law, and a Fatwa Council reviews laws, so religion and state are not strictly separated.

separated-powers.rationale: The declaration provides for separation of powers and judicial independence, but the president appoints ministers, the constitutional court and a third of the Assembly, so the record is contested.

single-official-language.rationale: His January 2026 decree names Kurdish a national language alongside Arabic and permits teaching in it, rather than making one language the sole common medium.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He said the president implements laws approved by the assembly and authority should rest in legal institutions.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: From December 2024 he folded rebel factions into the Defense Ministry, and the constitutional declaration he issued (Article 9) bars individuals and groups from forming armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He said Syria will not join any regional axis or become an arena for rival powers, while keeping strategic arms and energy ties with Russia and two Russian bases.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Freedom guarantees coexist with his criminalisation of pro-Assad speech and defence of HTS detentions against documented critics.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The declaration he issued lets religious communities keep their own personal status laws instead of one civil law for all.

women-suffrage.rationale: The declaration he issued commits the state to women's political rights, and the 2025 election decree set a target for women among electors; women stood in the October 2025 vote.

notes:
Positions changed sharply: answers use his most recent statements as president (2025-2026). His earlier jihadist statements were not the latest record on any answered topic. Many topics (social issues, taxes, welfare, most foreign policy) are null because he has made no direct statement; several later-reported items (Chatham House 2026) were reachable only through secondary summaries and were not used.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 19 answers taken from it, 19 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent full-list pass, no inference. Three priorities answered: regional neutrality, national culture and national rebirth. All other priorities remain null. Market adoption is not a theory of capitalism’s historical role. Avoiding specific wars is not absolute non-intervention; rejecting transit of arms is not a general foreign-insurgent funding doctrine. His personally commissioned constitution is distinguished from formal assent. Rights claims are qualified against appointment-controlled institutions and his own defence of earlier HTS detentions. Current abuses are not assumed his personal orders. Arabic text checked against the automated English translation. The August 2026 CNN broadcast repeats December 2025 remarks. The Atlantic Council’s automated transcript is used only for clear passages corroborated by Arabic interviews, excluding its erroneous age claim. Ecology and technology searches found no further matching positions. All 490 statements checked; main lane decides inclusion.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31) on line 14: searched his 2025 UN speech (UNGDC), the Constitutional Declaration's Arabic text (army, parties, presidential term, budget, transitional justice, environment), the 60 Minutes (Oct 2025), Amanpour (Dec 2025) and Atlantic Council (Sept 2026) interviews, and Arabic and English reporting on his portraits/personality cult, the ICC, borrowing for reconstruction, oil and gas output, and crony privileges. Added party-commands-army -1 medium and gradual-change -1 low. Left null: leader-cult (only reports of confiscated flags with his image, no statement of his), international-criminal-courts (he seeks Assad's trial 'by all legal means' and Syria has not joined the ICC), avoid-deficit-stimulus (his no-loans-for-reconstruction pledge is reported second-hand and concerns foreign borrowing, not deficit stimulus), expand-fossil-fuels (output targets are his ministers'), no-business-privileges (he denies economic power centres exist, a description not a position; Al-Khaleej original blocked), strong-leader and direct-election-head-of-state (he says authority is an institution not an individual and that every person will get one vote, but neither settles the statement), unlimited-reelection (the declaration sets no presidential term rule; he says he will stand). Most line-14 statements (ecology, technology, Marxist doctrine) have no record.
